ns2:section.sectionText: EALC 398—Tokyo: Then and Now More than four centuries old, Tokyo has been one of the largest most dynamic cities in the world for much of its history. Originally called Edo when it was the castle town and headquarters for the Tokugawa Shoguns, today Tokyo has grown into the modern megalopolis that is home and haunt to many icons of Japanese popular culture. In this course, you will be introduced to Edo-Tokyo through maps and artwork of its urban form, its temple and residential architecture, its literary and culinary creativity (sushi and tempura were once street food here), its markets and marketplaces, its quaint neighborhoods and bustling city centers, and it place in film, manga, and anime. You will also create your own story of Edo-Tokyo by exploring a topic of your choice about the city’s fascinating history and culture.
